This handbook is temporary development documentation and is intentionally updated as systems become usable.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.1: Glass: 32 base PU. It has no independent Scale/Lift/Float hard cap.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.2: Quartz: 48 base PU. Chassis efficiency multiplies this output.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.3: Amethyst: 64 base PU. The same Core becomes more capable in a more efficient chassis.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.4: Diamond: 96 base PU. Standard raw-material Cores use a ×1.00 Core amplification multiplier.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.5: Netherite: 128 base PU. A loaded Core Booster keeps the inserted material Base PU and amplifies it by ×1.50. Empty Boosters are not valid projector Cores.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.1: Import PNG, JPG/JPEG, static WebP, BMP or animated GIF. Mirage detects the real format from file bytes, not the extension. Static images normalize to PNG; GIF keeps its animation.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.2: Current plane chassis expose Front and Back. Back may mirror Front, show Front readable, or use an independent image.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.3: Vertical Flip and Scanlines are image-specific controls and therefore live in this workspace instead of the primary GUI.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.4: Mirage Prism now stores independent North/East/South/West image faces. Same Source on All Faces copies North's asset reference without duplicating files.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.1: Click an item onto the virtual Snapshot slot. Mirage copies one serialized visual snapshot and never removes the real item.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.2: Blocks render as 3D blocks, ordinary items use their full 3D item model, and standalone armor targets equipped geometry on the invisible rig.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.3: Clearing the virtual slot deletes only the snapshot. There is no obtainable stored item to steal or duplicate.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.1: Craft an Empty Scan Template with paper surrounded by eight iron nuggets, then Shift + right-click one living entity or player. Mirage gives this deliberate scan gesture priority over the target interaction.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.2: Humanoid scans expose Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Main Hand and Off Hand Incoming/Projected channels. Accepting a physical staging item returns the real item immediately; leaving the workspace also returns every leftover staging item, dropping overflow safely.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.3: Horse scans expose Saddle and Body Armor channels. Generic entities keep unsupported visual equipment inside the frozen entity snapshot.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.4: Humanoid projections have persistent pose presets. Pose changes the virtual rig only; scanned body and equipment snapshots stay untouched.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.5: Pose-aware preview fitting and conservative clearance reserve extra room for raised or spread arms.
Scale preserves the source aspect/model proportions. Lift moves the lowest projected point above the emitter.
Rotation controls period, direction and orientation. Floating controls amplitude and either time-cycle or rotation-synced timing.
Ghost Effect changes transparency. Tint applies a hologram color multiplier. Fullbright ignores world light.
Projection Power and clearance must both pass. Creative Debug chassis override removes chassis overdrive penalties for testing but never creates Core PU or bypasses the effective capacity budget.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.title: Development / Known Boundaries
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.1: Prism is functional for Image and Banner faces. Wide and Tall optionally support 4-source layouts; Field is a single continuous large Plane. Effigy and Colossal remain future chassis contracts.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.2: Optional backpack/accessory/artifact integrations are outside the base scope and will be adapters after the core systems stabilize.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.3: Humanoid pose presets are implemented. Special renderer compatibility and exact species-aware Entity bounds still need refinement.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.4: If a renderer cannot safely support a feature, Mirage should fall back rather than silently corrupt shared render state.

handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: The main projector screen controls presentation. Source workspaces decide what is projected: Image, Item Snapshot, Entity / Humanoid or Banner.
Standard Core base output is Glass 32 PU, Quartz 48 PU, Amethyst 64 PU, Diamond 96 PU and Netherite 128 PU. A loaded Core Booster preserves that Base PU and adds ×1.50 amplification.

Effective capacity = Core base PU × chassis multiplier × Core amplification. Chassis multipliers are Compact ×1.00, Display ×1.50, Wide ×2.00, Tall ×2.00, Field ×4.00 and Prism ×2.00. Standard Cores use ×1.00; loaded Core Boosters use ×1.50.

Chassis geometry, Lift and Float numbers are nominal efficiency targets, not hard walls. Going past nominal is legal if enough PU exists, but that component receives a squared overdrive penalty so the correct larger chassis remains much more efficient.

PU load is explicit: a non-empty projection pays 2 PU base; geometry pays about 1 PU per 16×16 projected pixels; Lift pays 1 PU per 16px; Float pays 1 PU per 2px; source complexity and enabled effects add small fixed costs. Each component is then overdrive-adjusted when it exceeds its chassis nominal target.

Ghost gives only a tiny efficiency rebate: floor(non-base gross PU × Ghost% / 3000). Even at the 90% Ghost maximum this can never save more than 3% of the non-base load, so transparency cannot be abused as a power strategy.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.compac: Use Compact for tiny local holograms and desk-sized displays where footprint matters more than efficiency at large sizes.
Nominal targets: 10×10 px, 32 px Lift, 4 px Float, 1 source. Power multiplier: ×1.00.

Compact can overdrive beyond 10×10 with a strong Core, but its cost rises quickly. A Netherite Core can therefore rival the effective PU budget of a Field with Glass while still being less efficient for massive geometry.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.displa: Use Display as the balanced general-purpose single-source projector when Compact is too small but a specialised chassis is unnecessary.
Nominal targets: 32×32 px, 48 px Lift, 12 px Float, 1 source. Power multiplier: ×1.50.
Display reaches readable medium-sized holograms efficiently and can still overdrive when extra PU is available.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.1: Use Wide for horizontal signs, panoramas and side-by-side content. It is tuned for landscape geometry.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.2: Nominal targets: 80×32 px, 64 px Lift, 12 px Float. Power multiplier: ×2.00. Image Mode toggles one continuous SINGLE source or four equivalent 4×1 cells; SINGLE preserves aspect ratio and horizontal content is naturally most efficient.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.3: Image Mode toggles between one continuous wide image and a 4×1 layout. MULTI uses four equal square cells; Scale 80 gives a complete 80×20 layout of four 20×20 cells, matching Tall cell sizing.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.1: Use Tall for vertical signage, portrait art, banner-like displays and stacked content where height matters more than width.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.2: Nominal targets: 32×80 px, 96 px Lift, 16 px Float. Power multiplier: ×2.00. Image Mode toggles one continuous SINGLE source or four equivalent 1×4 cells; SINGLE preserves aspect ratio and vertical content is naturally most efficient.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.3: Image Mode toggles between one continuous tall image and a 1×4 stack. MULTI uses the same square-cell rule as Wide; Scale 80 gives 20×80 overall, preventing the old Tall-vs-Wide magnification mismatch.
Use Field for one massive continuous planar image or large wall-scale display. It is the high-efficiency chassis for very large 2D geometry.
Nominal targets: 128×128 px, 144 px Lift, 24 px Float, 1 continuous Plane source. Power multiplier: ×4.00.
Field never uses a 3×3 image grid. The accidental dev.33-dev.37 grid interpretation is deprecated and migrated back to a single continuous Plane.
Use Prism for a freestanding display readable from several directions instead of a single flat front/back plane.

Prism always keeps four cardinal lateral faces (North/East/South/West), one image or GIF per face and no stacking mode. Per-face nominal geometry adapts to content: horizontal 80×32, vertical 32×80, near-square 48×48. Lift nominal 96 px, Float 12 px, power multiplier ×2.00.
Image and Banner modes expose world-cardinal North, East, South and West faces. Prism has no top or bottom image face. Each populated face contributes geometry load.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Scale, Lift and Float sliders are generated dynamically from the current effective PU budget. Their endpoint is the highest currently valid value, so you should not need to drag through an orange invalid range and search backward pixel by pixel.
tooltip.mirage_projector.image.layout_mo: Wide/Tall: SINGLE preserves the full source aspect ratio; horizontal content is natural for Wide and vertical for Tall. MULTI uses four equal square cells: Wide 4×1, Tall 1×4.
tooltip.mirage_projector.scale.dynamic: Scale ends at the largest value the current effective PU capacity can sustain. Going beyond the chassis nominal size is allowed as overdrive and becomes progressively more expensive.
tooltip.mirage_projector.lift.dynamic: Lift ends at the largest value the current effective PU capacity can sustain. Going beyond nominal Lift is overdrive and receives a quadratic cost penalty.
tooltip.mirage_projector.float.dynamic: Float ends at the largest value the current effective PU capacity and current Lift can sustain. Going beyond nominal Float is overdrive and receives a quadratic cost penalty.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Image assets are synchronized by SHA-256 asset ID. Static PNG/JPEG/WebP/BMP imports normalize to PNG; GIF keeps animation. Mirage detects format from file bytes, so renamed GIFs still animate and unsupported animated WebP/APNG are rejected instead of flattened.

Plane Image modes are explicit: Front shows only Front; Back shows only Back; Mirrored reuses Front as a mirror; Readable reuses Front with corrected rear orientation; Independent uses separate Front and Back assets. Clearance must also pass before rendering.

handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Crying Obsidian is renewable after you obtain a real block: place a Lava source directly above Crying Obsidian and leave space below. It can nucleate a downward Small Bud, then grow through Medium, Large and Mature stages; the first nucleation is deliberately the slowest step.

Without Silk Touch, Small/Medium/Large/Mature crystals drop exactly 1/2/3/4 Crying Obsidian Shards and Fortune does not increase them. Silk Touch preserves the current crystal stage for decoration or relocation.

An active Beacon can energize Crying Obsidian crystals. Small/Medium/Large transmit about 75%/50%/25% of the visual beam; Mature visually stops it while Beacon effects remain active. Energized crystals glow and leak narrow purple residual rays.

handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Obsidian Spikes are crafted from 3 Crying Obsidian Shards, 2 String and 1 Stick. Their nine sharp points slow living creatures like a berry bush and deal 2 damage points (1 heart) on each successful hurt event while the victim moves through them.

handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Projectors now form one crafting family: build the Compact Mirage Projector first, upgrade it to Mirage Display, then specialize that Display into Wide, Tall, Prism or Field. There is no direct Compact-to-specialist shortcut.

Breaking a projector normally in Survival packs its complete saved state into the dropped machine. Crafting upgrades carry that state forward, including the installed Core, imported images/GIFs, cards, snapshots and presentation settings.
